newsitem.title: GERMANY: World cotton supply-demand seen balanced in 97/98.
newsitem.headline: World cotton supply-demand seen balanced in 97/98.

text.p: Global cotton production and consumption should each rise to 19.49 million tonnes in 1997/98 (Aug-July) from 18.96 and 18.92 million respectively in 1996/97, the Bremen Cotton Exchange said.
The global cotton area should expand to 34.2 million hectares from 33.57 million in 1996/97, the exchange's annual report said.
China would seek to expand the national area and yields in Central Asia and Pakistan would be higher.
China might halve its imports in 1997/98 to 200,000 tonnes.
But world prices in the new season might be buoyed by stockbuilding outside China and reductions in Central Asian barter trade.
Bremen, Europe's leading cotton port, expected a consolidation in domestic textile production in 1997, boosted by exports.
Output had fallen last year in a weaker economic environment. Depreseed consumer spending had resulted in textile sales falling by 1.7 percent to 31.5 billion marks.
Cotton yarn spinning dropped 5.5 percent to 126,540 tonnes.
German net imports of cotton in 1996 were up by 0.4 percent at 142,497 tonnes but their value dropped 4.6 percent to 383 million marks.
